topic: Agent-shell 2026: Vendor-Neutral Chat with AI Agents from Emacs

key_points: agent-shell is a native Emacs shell powered by comint-mode, so no dancing between char/line modes
Agent-agnostic thanks to ACP (Agent Client Protocol) — configure any agent via a common protocol
Shows Gemini CLI vs Claude Code config examples with acp-make-client
Traffic buffer (M-x agent-shell-view-traffic) to inspect ACP JSON traffic
Fake agents: save traffic to disk and replay it for cheap, fast testing
Built on acp.el, an Emacs Lisp implementation of ACP developed between Zed and Google
agent-shell enters the chat: chat mode fuses comint with traditional chat-like labelling, enabled by default (disable via agent-shell-chat-mode-enabled nil)
Activity grouping: tool calls and thinking collapsed by default; expand via agent-shell-activity-group-expand-by-default, or 'latest for only-latest-expanded
Prompt queueing consolidated under agent-shell-prompt-queue.el (queue, resume, remove)
M-x agent-shell-prompt-compose lets you craft prompts from any buffer; C-c C-c fire-and-forget, C-u C-c C-c queue another
Shell prompts offered as soon as possible so you can start typing during init
Markdown lists get normalized padding/indentation; TAB navigation + hints for source blocks, links, images
New agents: Oh My Pi (omp) and Grok Build (xAI); Cursor now on official Cursor CLI (agent acp)
Codex now uses @agentclientprotocol/codex-acp; Goose no longer requires OpenAI key by default
agent-shell-preferred-agent-config for finer agent selection (skip picker or preselect)
Custom markdown renderers via agent-shell-markdown-render-functions (e.g. agent-shell-math-renderer renders LaTeX as SVG)
agent-shell-faces.el for theming control; less chatter via tool/thinking grouping
Native Emacs shell to interact with LLM agents powered by ACP (Agent Client Protocol)
~1,824 stars, 229 forks, Emacs Lisp, actively updated (Sep 2026)

Supports 18+ agents: Claude Agent, Codex, Gemini CLI, Goose, Grok Build, Cursor, Kimi Code CLI, CodeBuddy, Kiro CLI, Qwen Code, Auggie, Mistral Vibe, Factory Droid, Pi, Oh My Pi, Opencode, Antigravity
Install via MELPA: (use-package agent-shell :ensure t); deps acp.el and shell-maker

Rich ecosystem of companion packages: emacs-skills, agent-shell-sidebar, agent-shell-bookmark, agent-shell-workspace, agent-shell-manager, agent-review, ob-agent-shell (Org Babel), agent-shell-tramp, agent-shell-dashboard, agent-shell-hq, etc.
Image utilities: clipboard paste (pngpaste/wl-paste/xclip) and screenshots per platform
ACP standardizes communication between code editors/IDEs and coding agents, suitable for local and remote
Solves integration overhead, limited compatibility, and developer lock-in
Similar to how LSP standardized language server integration
Local agents run as sub-processes communicating via JSON-RPC over stdio; remote via HTTP/WebSocket (work in progress)
Developed between Zed and Google; v1 stable, v2 draft; libraries in Kotlin, Java, Python, Rust, TypeScript

stats.fact: agent-shell has ~1,824 GitHub stars and 229 forks as of September 2026
agent-shell supports 18+ ACP-driven agents including Claude Agent, Codex, Gemini CLI, Goose, Grok Build, Cursor, Qwen Code, Mistral Vibe, and Opencode
The original 'Introducing Emacs agent-shell' post drew 233 points on Hacker News (Oct 2025)

agent-shell and its dependency acp.el are both available on MELPA

angles: Vendor-neutrality: one Emacs buffer, any agent — the ACP protocol is the key unlock, not any single vendor
2026 state of the art: chat mode, activity grouping, prompt queueing, compose-from-anywhere — agent-shell has matured from a shell into a full chat experience
The ACP ecosystem: 18+ agents and a growing companion-package ecosystem (skills, sidebar, bookmarks, Org Babel, Tramp, dashboards)
Local-first and privacy: run agents locally (e.g. Opencode + local Ollama Qwen2.5:7b) entirely from Emacs
Practical setup: install via MELPA, configure auth via environment variables, pick your preferred agent
Why ACP matters: solves integration overhead, limited compatibility, and developer lock-in — the LSP moment for AI agents
